response.title: which power station gives you the most of its advertised capacity in real use
response.answer:
The best portable power station isn't necessarily the one with the largest advertised battery. It's the one that delivers the highest percentage of its rated watt-hours (Wh) to your devices.

For example, a 1,000 Wh power station that delivers 920 Wh has a 92% usable-capacity ratio. Another rated at 1,000 Wh might deliver only 800 Wh.

The important distinction is how you're drawing power:

AC output (wall outlets): Typically less efficient because the inverter consumes energy converting battery DC power to AC.

DC output (USB-C or 12V): Often more efficient because it avoids the main AC inverter.

Low-power loads: Can be surprisingly inefficient, especially when the inverter stays on for hours.

For comparing brands, I'd prioritize independently measured AC usable capacity rather than manufacturer claims.
